youtube.title: The Bricks Aren't What Keep Water In
youtube.caption:
Why don't you dry out? Your skin has a brick wall.

That wall is the skin's first line of defence. It keeps outside things out and holds water in. It is not a single tough sheet. It is a system of cells, fats and acids. So your skin's wall is bricks and fats, working as a team. The fats are the seal.

Series: Season 2: What your skin does, part 5 of 6. Next: fingerprints, formed before birth

Sources
1. The permeability barrier function of the stratum corneum (SC) is provided by lipid lamellae surrounding corneocytes; the protective cutaneous functions largely reside in the SC. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17313091/
2. The skin barrier is the first line of protection against pathogens, allergens and transepidermal water loss. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42955253/
3. Fingerprint ridges form in waves spreading from variable initiation sites, before birth. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36764291/

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Illustrations: AI-generated and 3-D animation made in code, no stock footage. Every number's source is listed in this description.

Education, not medical advice. See a dermatologist about your own skin.
